battle.name: 隋平李世賢叛亂
battle.brief: 開皇十七年（597年），隋平郡人李世賢聚眾起兵，據郡城與汴渠一線的漕運為亂，隋朝以郡兵據城、州郡策應、朝廷遣軍掃平，數月之間事定。卡面的埃及長矛屬早王朝青銅兵器，與本役相隔近四千年，並不在戰場之上；隋軍步兵實際所恃者為鐵矛長槊、環首刀、弓弩與巢車雲梯一類攻城器械。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場衝突是隋文帝開皇十七年（597年）發生在河南道隋平郡境內的一場郡級叛亂，交戰的一方是隋朝中央與其河南道的郡縣官署，另一方是聚眾起事的隋平郡人李世賢所率部眾。隋朝一方在名義上握有天下：自開皇元年受北周禪讓之後，楊堅在二十年間建立起以州郡為骨架、以戶籍與租調為經脈的統治，府兵與宿衛並存的兵制也已成形；一旦地方有事，郡兵可先據城固守，鄰州郡兵隨即赴援，朝廷再視情形加派行軍總管率京師武衛出討，這套由上而下、由近及遠的動員程序，是開皇年間各次平叛的常態。叛亂一方則完全沒有制度後盾，起事者靠的是鄉里關係、獵戶與逃戶的武裝，以及對本地山川道路的熟悉，起事初期多以襲擊縣鎮、截斷糧道與劫掠官署為主要手段，人數有限但行動迅速。隋平郡的位置尤為關鍵：其治所在陳州陽夏，即今河南周口一帶，控汝水、淮水與蔡水之間的沖積平原，又緊鄰汴渠與通濟渠的漕運線，郡兵、糧車與文書的往來在此交會，這使它既容易成為聚眾截道的目標，也容易在郡兵與援軍合圍之下被迅速壓平。與此同時，周邊的汝南、襄城、潁川等州郡在名義上仍屬朝廷一方，其態度與糧秣供應直接決定叛亂能撐多久；北邊的突厥與東邊的高句麗方向上，隋朝邊軍正在備戰，可隨時抽調的兵馬有限。
countriesEn: This conflict was a commandery-level rebellion that broke out inside Suiping Commandery, in Henan Circuit, in the seventeenth year of the Kaihuang era (597 CE), under the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui. One side was the Sui central court together with the commandery and county offices of Henan Circuit; the other was the body of followers raised by Li Shixian, a native of Suiping. The Sui side nominally held the realm: after taking the abdication from Northern Zhou in the first year of Kaihuang, Yang Jian spent two decades building a state whose skeleton was the commandery-and-county system and whose lifeblood was household registration and the land and poll tax, and an order in which fubing troops and the palace guard coexisted had also taken shape. Whenever trouble arose locally, the commandery troops could hold the walled seat first, the neighbouring prefectures could bring up reinforcements, and the court could then, according to the scale of the affair, send a travelling generalissimus with the capital's wuwei guard to mop up. That top-down, near-to-far mobilisation sequence was the standard way disturbances were suppressed throughout the Kaihuang years. The rebel side had no institutional support whatever: the insurgents relied on village ties, on the arms of hunters and runaways, and on their intimate knowledge of the local hills, rivers and roads. In the opening phase their usual methods were to strike county seats, cut supply lines and seize government stores, so that their numbers stayed limited while their movements stayed fast. The position of Suiping Commandery matters here: its seat was at Yangxia in Zhou Prefecture, in the Zhoukou region of modern Henan, holding the alluvial plain between the Ru, Huai and Cai rivers and lying immediately beside the canal route formed by the Bian Canal and the Tongji Canal. Commandery troops, grain carts and official documents crossed there every day, which made it at once an easy place for gathering men to cut the road and a place that could be sealed quickly once commandery troops and relieving columns closed in. At the same time the neighbouring prefectures of Runan, Xiangcheng and Yingchuan remained, in name, on the court's side, and their attitude and their deliveries of grain and men decided how long the rising could hold out. To the north the Turks and to the east the Goguryeo front were already absorbing the court's attention, so the troops that could be detached for a local operation were limited.
people: 可考的相關人物不算多，這場叛亂在正史中只留下寥寥數筆。叛方首領李世賢，籍屬隋平郡，《隋書》僅記其起兵為亂，姓名之外的事蹟、出身與所聚人數都沒有交代，後世也無從考其家世與郡內是否另有豪族為之後盾，因此對他的定位只能停留在「郡中之豪、聚眾抗命者」的層次。朝廷方面的最高決策者是隋文帝楊堅，開皇十七年他治下已行有餘年，而其統治的關鍵在於「郡先守、州後援、朝廷再遣大軍」的處置次序，這一政策在他即位後的多次叛亂中都反覆使用。楊廣於開皇年間出任河南道行台尚書令，駐節洛陽，總督河南諸州軍事與刑名，正好是隋平郡所屬的上一級軍政樞紐；若事勢擴大，調兵與調糧的第一道轉軸就在他手上。宰相蘇威等人則在政事堂層面維持朝廷的常態運作。討平叛亂的將領姓名在現存記載中並不清晰，只能確定朝廷確實派出一支討叛的部隊，其規模與路線今人已難考訂；地方上，隋平郡丞、縣令與郡兵都尉屬於臨機應變的第一線，郡兵一旦潰散或倒戈，整個平叛的進度就會完全改變。從《隋書·高祖紀》以月份為經的編年體例看，起事、朝廷發兵與平定之間的間隔很短，這說明參與處置的並非什麼名將，而是一套運作成熟的郡縣與行軍總管體制。
peopleEn: Few people can be documented for this rising; the official histories leave it only a few lines. On the rebel side the leader was Li Shixian, a native of Suiping Commandery. The History of Sui records only that he raised troops in revolt: nothing is said of his career, his family or the number of men he gathered, and no later source allows us to trace his origins or to establish whether other local powerful families stood behind him, so he can be placed no further than a notable of the commandery who gathered men and defied the government. The supreme decision-maker on the court side was Yang Jian, Emperor Wen of Sui, who by the seventeenth year of Kaihuang had governed for some time; the key to his method lay in the sequence of commandery first holds the city, prefecture next brings relief, court then dispatches a major column, a policy applied repeatedly to the disturbances of his reign. During the Kaihuang years Yang Guang served as Henan Circuit's Xingtaishangshuling, resident at Luoyang and supervising military and civil administration across the Henan prefectures, and Luoyang was precisely the theatre-level hinge to which Suiping belonged; had the affair widened, the first point of leverage for shifting troops and grain lay in his hands. Su Wei and the other ministers kept the routine machinery of government running at the level of the Secretariat. The name of the commander who finally put the rising down is not clear in the surviving record; all that can be established is that the court did send out a force to deal with it, while its size and its route of march can no longer be reconstructed. At local level the assistant officer of Suiping Commandery, the county magistrates and the commandery troop commander were the first line of response, and if the commandery troops broke or turned coat the entire course of the suppression would have changed. The way the Annals of the High Emperor in the History of Sui is arranged, month by month, shows only a short interval between the rising, the dispatch of troops and the ending, which means no celebrated general was involved; what handled the affair was a mature system of commanderies, counties and travelling generalissimi.
kits: 卡面上這件兵器是「埃及長矛」，一件早王朝時期的青銅長矛，年代遠在隋代之前三千八百餘年，史料中不會出現在隋平郡的任何一次交鋒裡；把它放進這場戰爭，是就「長矛」這一兵器類別所作的圖解。它的形制要點在青銅矛頭與木杆的結合：直刃、無血槽，形制簡單而便於成列使用，握在手中可刺可挑，必要時也能投擲，早王朝的埃及人把它用於守護城垣與收復失地的隊伍之中。放到開皇十七年的河南，這種「直刃矛配木杆」的邏輯正是隋軍步兵的基本配備：隋軍近戰以鐵矛、長槊為骨幹，輔以環首刀、鎗、鐗與鉤，弓弩手居前射擊，長兵手在後列陣，與埃及長矛在功能上同屬把射擊極限之後那一線距離重新拉回正面的兵器。圍城與野戰中，隋朝一方還有巢車、雲梯、版築、撞車、橹車與拒馬、鹿角等器械，以及夯土城垣與木柵一類守城設施；叛方所能倚仗的則是鄉里自備的弓箭、削尖的竹木、耒耜、繩索與田間工具改造成的簡單器械。外圍的後勤依賴牛車、馬匹馱運與隋朝在河南新開的運河水道，把洛陽、汴州的糧秣沿汴渠送到陳、蔡一線。卡面之外，與這場戰爭真正相關的裝備，其實是隋軍那一整套冷兵器組合。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face is the Egyptian spear, a bronze-age spear of the early dynastic period, more than three thousand eight hundred years older than the Sui, which cannot appear in any clash fought at Suiping; placing it in this war is a diagrammatic gesture towards the category of the spear. Its defining feature is the combination of a bronze head with a wooden shaft: a straight blade without a fuller, simple enough to be ranked in files, capable in the hand of stabbing and hooking and, if need be, of being thrown, and the early dynastic Egyptians used it in the columns that guarded city walls and recovered lost ground. Set in the Henan of the seventeenth year of Kaihuang, the same logic of a straight-bladed head on a wooden shaft is exactly the basic equipment of Sui infantry: in close combat the Sui relied on iron spears and long mao as their backbone, supported by ring-pommel sabres, halberds, long-handled axes and hooks, with crossbow and bow men shooting from the front and the polearm ranks formed behind, so that in functional terms the Egyptian spear belonged to the same family of weapons that pulled the line beyond effective range back into the open. In siege and field work the Sui also had siege-towers, scaling ladders, ramps, battering rams, mobile sheds, cheval-de-frise and spiked barriers, together with rammed-earth walls and palisades as field fortifications; all the rebels could rely on were village bows, sharpened bamboo and wood, hoes, ploughshares, rope and simple tools of the fields turned into weapons. On the periphery, logistics depended on ox carts, on pack animals, and on the new waterways opened by the Sui in Henan, moving grain and provisions from Luoyang and Bianzhou to the Chen and Cai lines. Beyond the card face, the equipment genuinely related to this war was the Sui army's whole ensemble of cold weapons.
tactics: 因為正史對此役的記載極簡，戰術只能從隋朝平叛的通例與當地地形推出大致輪廓。叛軍的典型動作有三：一是趁郡兵交接、縣令交接的空檔突然聚眾，先占縣城、驛舍與糧倉，切斷汴渠、汝水一線的運輸；二是利用淮北平原的開闊地形與村邑密集的特點，把隊伍分散成小股，避開隋軍主力，專打郡兵巡隊、運輸隊與落單人馬；三是在官軍逼近時退入鄉里堅壁，或順勢散入民間，使官軍失去可以攻打的目標。隋軍這邊的戰術要點是「以郡守城、以州策應、以軍掃清」：先由郡兵據城固守，閉門拒守同時急報州府；州刺史調集鄰郡之兵在城下結營，築營柵、掘壕塹、配備衝車與雲梯，把叛軍壓在城郊；朝廷再派行軍總管率京師宿衛與河南諸州兵循糧道推進，兵鋒不急於攻坚，而是先斷糧道、掃清鄉野，最後才以器械攻城，或以招撫令降者免罪、脅從者遣散，把聚眾解散在械鬥之前。糧秣與文書的調度同樣是戰術的一部分：隋朝的漕運線沿汴渠、通濟渠與淮、汝諸水運轉，叛軍只要卡住河道與驛道，隋軍就得改走陸路、耗費倍增；反過來，隋軍保住這條線，就等於保住這場平叛的血液。季節上，開皇十七年的河南仍在秋收之前，若戰事拖到收割之後，糧道的季節性壓力會更明顯。
tacticsEn: Because the official record of this operation is extremely terse, its tactics can only be sketched from the Sui's general practice in suppressing risings and from the local terrain. The rebels had three characteristic moves. First, they gathered men in the gap between the handover of commandery troops or of county magistrates, seizing county seats, post stations and granaries and cutting the traffic along the Bian Canal and the Ru river. Second, they used the openness of the northern Huai plain and the density of villages to break their force into small bands that avoided the Sui main body and struck instead at commandery patrols, supply convoys and isolated men. Third, when the government troops closed in they withdrew into the villages to stand behind walls, or simply dispersed among the people, leaving the government without a target it could attack. On the Sui side the tactical formula was: the commandery holds the city, the prefecture provides the response, the army cleans up. Commandery troops first held the walled seat, refusing entry and sending urgent reports to the prefectural office in parallel. The prefect then mustered the neighbouring commanderies' troops into camps below the city, raising stockades, digging trenches and providing battering rams and scaling ladders so as to pin the rebels close to the walls. The court then sent a travelling generalissimus with the capital's guard and the troops of the Henan prefectures to advance along the supply route; his priority was not to storm the defences at once but to cut the grain road, to clear the countryside, and only at the end to bring up the siege equipment, or to offer amnesty to those who came out and to disband the coerced, dissolving the gatherings before any clash of arms. The movement of grain and documents was itself part of the tactics: the Sui supply line ran along the Bian Canal, the Tongji Canal and the waters of the Huai and the Ru, and if the rebels blocked a waterway or a post road the Sui would be forced onto roads and their costs would double. Put the other way, by keeping that line the Sui kept the blood supply of the whole suppression. As for season, the harvest in Henan of the seventeenth year of Kaihuang still lay ahead, and had the fighting dragged on past the harvest the seasonal pressure on the supply route would have become far more acute.
data: 可以確定的數字有限，但仍有幾項可作座標。第一是時間：開皇十七年即公元597年，隋文帝在位的第二十一年；開皇是隋文帝的年號，自581年改元至600年改元仁壽，共二十年。第二是地望：隋平郡屬河南道，治所在陳州陽夏縣，即今河南省周口市淮陽區一帶，郡境處於西面近汝水、東面接淮水與蔡水之間的沖積平原，領陽夏、項城、臨蔡、新蔡等縣，治所距東都洛陽約三百里，漕運則經汴渠與通濟渠與洛陽相通。第三是編制：隋朝在開皇年間的全國戶籍約四百六十餘萬戶、戶口約二千萬上下，這是依《隋書·食貨志》與開皇十年大索貌閱前後的籍帳推算的概數；府兵仍是京師宿衛與邊防的骨幹，地方州郡另有供差遣的常備兵與鄉里武裝，京師則有武衛、虎賁等宿衛大軍。第四是本役本身：現存史料只留下「起兵」與「平定」兩頭，中間的兵員數、交戰次數、進軍路線與耗損都沒有記載；一般而言，隋朝處理這類郡級叛亂所派出的部隊規模多在數千人上下，兵種以步騎混合的郡兵、州兵與京師宿衛為主，很少演成大規模會戰。此外還有一組可用的時間座標：隋朝在598年即開皇十八年第一次大舉征討高句麗，597年的河南正是這次用兵前籌措糧秣、徵發丁壯的年份，本役應放在這個背景下理解。關於起事者的具體人數與所據城邑，至今沒有可靠數字可引，本檔只作「郡內起事、數月之內平定」的定性描述，不作僭越的估計。
dataEn: The figures that can be established with certainty are few, but several still serve as coordinates. First, time: the seventeenth year of Kaihuang is 597 CE, the twenty-first year of Emperor Wen of Sui's reign; Kaihuang was the reign title of Emperor Wen, used from the change of era in 581 until the change to Renshou in 600, a total of twenty years. Second, place: Suiping Commandery belonged to Henan Circuit, with its seat at Yangxia county in Zhou Prefecture, in the Huaiyang region of modern Zhoukou in Henan; the commandery lay on the alluvial plain between the Ru river on the west and the Huai and Cai rivers on the east, and comprised counties including Yangxia, Xiangcheng, Lincai and Xincai; the seat was roughly three hundred li from the eastern capital Luoyang, and the canal traffic between the two ran through the Bian Canal and the Tongji Canal. Third, organisation: the household registers of the Sui in the Kaihuang years amount to a little over 4.6 million households and some twenty million people, a round figure estimated from the Treatise on the Economy of the History of Sui and from the registers surveyed around the great registration of the tenth year of Kaihuang; fubing troops remained the backbone of the capital's guard and the frontier garrisons, the prefectures and commanderies had their own standing troops for assignment together with village levies, and the capital maintained large guard units such as the wuwei and the hubei. Fourth, the operation itself: the surviving sources give only the outbreak and the suppression, and say nothing of the numbers engaged, the number of clashes, the route of march or the losses; as a general rule, the force the Sui sent against risings of this commandery scale was on the order of several thousand, mixed foot and horse drawn from commandery troops, prefectural troops and the capital's guard, and it seldom developed into a pitched battle. A further set of usable time coordinates: the Sui launched its first great campaign against Goguryeo in 598, the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, and the Henan of 597 was precisely the year in which grain was being stockpiled and labour levies raised for that campaign, which is the context in which this rising should be read. As for the number of the insurgents and the specific seats they occupied, no reliable figure survives; this file therefore gives only the qualitative description of a rising raised within one commandery and put down within a few months, and makes no improper estimate.
cause: 叛亂的起因沒有留下任何直接說明，只能從隋文帝治下中期的政策與河南一處的處境去推想。第一層是制度層面的推進：開皇三年到十年之間，隋朝在全國推行州郡制整頓、輸籍定樣與大索貌閱，括核戶口、均定田畝、重定租調與徭役的負擔。這套措施對國家的財政與兵源都是必要的，但它同時意味著大量隱戶重新被登記進簿籍，鄉里自耕者第一次要面對國家的直接抽取。開皇末年，隋朝同時在北方與突厥、在東北與高句麗兩線用兵，徵丁、轉糧、築城、備船的任務一齊壓到河南一帶的州縣身上，陳、蔡地界的民戶既是運河沿線的納糧戶，又是丁壯與畜力的來源。第二層是災患與糧價：開皇中期以後河南的郡縣屢見水旱記載，漕運線上的物資調度因此更形緊張，災後的流民、逃戶與失地者往往聚在陳、汝一帶，成為起事最現成的人力。第三層是地理與機會：隋平郡既在汴渠與通濟渠的轉運線上，郡兵、糧車與文書每日往返，一旦郡內出現裂痕，截斷一條驛道或一座糧倉的成本極低。第四層是朝廷的處置方式：隋文帝對起事一向嚴懲，但同時在開皇十年以後屢次採取明示赦宥、脅從遣散的辦法，這使小規模的郡級叛亂往往在郡級層面就被消化，也使同一批起事者反覆經歷聚眾、受撫、再聚的循環。起事者未必有什麼完整的政治主張，多數只是把對於徭役、括戶與徵丁的不滿，轉化為對郡兵與糧道的直接行動。
causeEn: No direct explanation of the outbreak survives, so the causes can only be inferred from the policies of the middle Kaihuang years and from the condition of one region of Henan. The first layer is institutional: between the third and the tenth year of Kaihuang the Sui carried out a nationwide tightening of the commandery-and-county system, the regulation of household registers and the great registration of the population, checking households, equalising fields and resetting the burden of tax and corvée. All of this was necessary to the state's finances and its supply of soldiers, but it also meant that a large number of concealed households were written back into the registers, and that village cultivators now faced direct claims from the state for the first time. In the later Kaihuang years the Sui was fighting on two fronts at once, against the Turks in the north and against Goguryeo in the northeast, and the tasks of levying men, moving grain, building walls and equipping ships all fell at once on the prefectures and commanderies of Henan. The households of the Chen and Cai regions were thus at once the grain-delivering population along the canal and the source of labour and draught animals. The second layer is calamity and prices: from the middle Kaihuang years the prefectures of Henan repeatedly appear in the record with floods and droughts, the material traffic on the canal route grew correspondingly strained, and the displaced, the runaways and the landless of the disaster years gathered along the Chen and the Ru, providing the most readily available manpower for a rising. The third layer is geography and opportunity: Suiping lay on the transshipment line of the Bian and Tongji canals, where commandery troops, grain carts and documents passed every day, so that once a fissure opened inside the commandery, cutting a post road or emptying a granary cost very little. The fourth layer is the court's own way of handling such affairs: Emperor Wen was always severe with risings, but from the tenth year of Kaihuang onward he repeatedly combined severity with public amnesty and the disbanding of the coerced, which meant that small commandery-level risings were often absorbed at commandery level, and that the same men went through repeated cycles of gathering, being pardoned and gathering again. The insurgents need not have held any complete political programme; most of them simply turned their resentment at corvée, at the checking of households and at the levying of men into direct action against the commandery troops and the grain roads.
impact: 就當時而言，這場叛亂的規模與影響都很有限，卻正好可以用來量度隋文帝時期地方秩序的實際狀態。第一，它說明開皇年間的中央集權已經落到郡縣層面：郡兵能據城、州兵能策應、朝廷能派宿衛下來，這條鏈條一旦運轉，隋朝就有能力在數月之內把任何郡級起事壓回原位，不必動用傾國的兵力和長期的圍城消耗。第二，它反過來說明隋朝的統治仍帶有自上而下的痕跡：平叛依靠的是行政體系的強制力，而不是地方社會的內生認同；被解散的起事者回到田間之後，並不會因此消除對括戶與徵丁的不滿，只是失去了再次集結的契機。第三，在財政與軍務上，本役的耗用微乎其微，隋朝在開皇年間仍保有充盈的府庫與穩定的糧道，這正是它能夠在598年隨即發動第一次征高句麗戰爭的底氣所在；開皇末年那些被平定的地方叛亂，與其說是危機，不如說是中央有餘力的證明。第四，在史學上，這類只留下兩行記載的事件本身就是資料：《隋書·高祖紀》以年月排比國事，起事與平定各佔一行，說明在隋文帝治下地方大規模兵亂已非常態，這與隋末那種郡縣各自徵兵、跨州連郡、延續十餘年的割據亂局形成了極為強烈的對照。第五，對後世歷史書寫而言，像李世賢這樣只有姓名的起事首領，說明在隋書的敘事中，郡級叛亂的價值不在人物，而在制度層面的秩序維持；它們被壓平之後就歸入編年的一行，不再需要更多的篇幅。
impactEn: In the context of the time the scale and the effect of this rising were both very limited, yet it serves well to measure the actual condition of local order under Emperor Wen. First, it shows that centralisation in the Kaihuang years had already reached the level of the commandery and the county: commandery troops could hold a city, prefectural troops could respond, and the court could send down the palace guard; once that chain was turning, the Sui was able to push any commandery-level rising back into place within a few months, without expending the resources of a nation or a prolonged siege. Second, it shows in reverse that Sui rule still carried the mark of being imposed from above: suppression rested on the coercive force of the administrative system and not on the spontaneous consent of local society, and once the insurgents were disbanded and returned to their fields, their resentment at the checking of households and the levying of men did not disappear; only the occasion to gather again was removed. Third, in fiscal and military terms the cost of this operation was negligible. The Sui in the Kaihuang years still held full treasuries and a stable supply route, and that was precisely the reserve that allowed it to open the first campaign against Goguryeo in 598; the local risings put down in the late Kaihuang years were, rather than crises, proof that the centre had strength to spare. Fourth, from the historian's point of view an event of this kind, preserved in two lines, is itself a datum: the Annals of the High Emperor in the History of Sui order the business of the realm by month and year, and the rising and its suppression each take a single line, which shows that large-scale local wars were no longer the normal condition under Emperor Wen. This forms a very sharp contrast with the late Sui, when commanderies raised their own troops, the fighting linked several prefectures into one, and the resulting fragmentation ran on for more than a decade. Fifth, for later historical writing, a rebel leader known only by a name such as Li Shixian shows that in the narrative of the History of Sui the significance of a commandery-level rising lay not in personalities but in the maintenance of order at the institutional level; once such risings were crushed they were folded into a single line of the annals and required nothing more.
result: 結果是隋朝平定了這場叛亂。起事者最終被解散與擒獲，隋平郡的城防與漕運秩序恢復，郡兵歸建制，郡丞與縣令照舊供職，朝廷沒有因此改封疆、沒有加征一次大賦，也沒有為此投入一支需要長期宿紮的部隊。從編年體例的記載方式看，從起兵到平定之間大約不過數月，跨越一個作戰季節之內，這說明整個過程並沒有演成需要攻城拔邑的會戰，而是以郡兵據守、州兵策應、官軍掃清，再加上招撫與赦宥的組合收場。叛首李世賢的下場在現存記載中並無明確交代，只能確定其部眾潰散、本人不再出現在隋初的官方記錄中，後世史家亦未留下追索其人的線索。就本役的最終意義而言，它是一次典型的郡級叛亂被中央體制快速吸收的案例：亂事起於一郡之地，終結於一郡之地，沒有改變隋朝北強南進的大局，也沒有在中原留下長期的割據基礎；它留下的，是開皇年間隋朝在地方控制上的一次成功檢驗，以及一條可供後人比對的註腳：當中央能夠同時握有行政命令與足量兵力的時候，任何以郡兵為骨幹的起事都難以走遠。
resultEn: The outcome was that the Sui put the rising down. The insurgents were eventually dispersed and taken, the defences and the canal traffic of Suiping Commandery returned to order, the commandery troops were re-established in their establishments, and the assistant officer and county magistrates resumed their posts; the court neither altered the boundaries nor levied a great additional tax, nor committed a force that would have had to quarter for a long time. Judging by the way the annals record it, only a few months separate the outbreak from the suppression, well inside a single campaigning season, which means the affair never developed into a battle requiring the storming of walled cities; it ended through a combination of commanderies holding the city, prefectures providing the response, government troops clearing the countryside, and then amnesty and pardon dissolving the gathered bands. What became of Li Shixian himself is not clearly recorded; all that can be established is that his following scattered and that he no longer appears in the official records of the early Sui, and that later historians left no trail by which he could be traced. As for the ultimate meaning of the operation, it is a typical case of a commandery-level rising being absorbed quickly by the central system: the trouble began in one commandery and ended in one commandery, it did not alter the balance by which the Sui grew strong in the north and pressed forward in the south, and it left no lasting base for separatism in the central plains. What it did leave was a successful test of the Sui's control of the localities in the Kaihuang years, and a note that later writers could set beside others: when the centre holds both the administrative command and an adequate supply of soldiers, no rising built on commandery troops can travel far.
